events.what: Bai, Shelukhin, Wang and Xu post a claimed proof of the Arnold–Givental conjecture in full generality
Hirschi and Porcelli announce an independent proof of Arnold–Givental at an Augsburg conference; no written argument located

judgement.doubts: The bullet names two conjectures; the record only addresses Arnold–Givental. The (strong) Arnold conjecture remains open, so even a verified BSWX proof would settle one part of the bullet. The Hirschi–Porcelli announcement is an oral talk with no public written argument, so it is not counted as an event. Pith's 'thin point' is automated review (F11), neither digestion nor knock-down.

corrections.why: F2/F1: the bullet is 'Arnold–Givental conjecture and Arnold conjecture'; the record's own summary says it 'center[s] on the Arnold–Givental half'. A proof of one of two named conjectures is scope 'case', which tiers to partial regardless of verification; the unreviewed status of the preprint does not make it 'claimed'.
